Keeping a homelab's backups honest

By a tester, 29 September 2026

A backup nobody has restored is a hope, not a backup. This post walks through the monthly drill that turns one into the other: pick a snapshot at random, restore it somewhere harmless, and compare what came back with what should have.

The drill

  1. Choose a snapshot older than a week, so the drill also proves retention works.
  2. Restore it into a scratch directory on a machine that is not the source.
  3. Compare checksums of a sample of files against the live copies.

The comparison is the part people skip. A restore that finishes without errors can still bring back empty files if the source was already corrupt when the snapshot ran.

What to record

FieldWhy
Snapshot ageRetention is part of the promise.
Restore timeIt sets how long an outage lasts.
 
restic restore latest --target /tmp/drill --include /srv/photos

Write the result down with the date. Next month's drill compares against it, and a restore that got slower is the first sign of a disk on its way out.
